messages.author: f79b33fe507b6757
messages.subject: Location error
parts:
Hi Chris, 

Thank you for your help!! I looked over the location error on the vignette you provided. My lemurs are recorded in 10-minute sample intervals within ten months. I don't have calibration data, so I follow the directions on "Simultaneous fitting with uncalibrated data."  My DOF=68-84 which is still low for ten months of tracking; as shown below:

[1] "OUF anisotropic error"

$DOF
    mean     area    speed 
68.94538 84.95954 10.23566 

$CI
                             low       est      high
area (hectares)        17.186252 21.517261 26.327624
τ[position] (hours)     4.006612  5.600196  7.827611
τ[velocity] (minutes)   1.477568  5.703811 22.018245
speed (kilometers/day)  3.551830  5.103356  6.652662
error (meters)         13.988632 17.243720 20.492437

If I am reading this correctly, my lemur's position is 5 hours, with two crossings per day. The velocity is the average the animal travels with the same speed and direction; however, I notice intervals are wide instead of narrow. Lastly, the error is showing me the impact of location error, which is 17 meters? Is this correct, and is this a good model to use? 

Thank you again for your help! I hope I am not confusing it too much, 
Jelisa

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Location error
parts:
Hi Jelisa,

If the data are broken up, how many ~4-8 hour intervals are recorded in the data? You expect DOF[mean] and DOF[area] to be on the order of that amount. Long gaps in the data do not provide any information. The other thing I would consider is how well the variograms match.

The velocity autocorrelation timescale CIs are wide because the data are coarsely sampled relative to that scale and there is substantial location error.

14-20 meter error is plausible for GPS. Does your data record HDOP? That could be useful for an arboreal species. Also if you have the ability to collect some calibration data.

Best,
Chris
